title: First seeing Louis Armstrong in 1923 and Johnny Dunn's put-down
summary: Howard first saw Armstrong in 1923 and tells how Johnny Dunn took Louis's horn and made him look bad.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When did you first see Louis?
When what? When did you first see Louis Armstrong? 1923. Now he's the one that played at Dreamland, that's his first job.

Uh-huh. Just one trumpet. Joe Oliver's over to the Royal Garden. I'll tell you something. You remember Johnny, what is trumpet player playing with Florence Mills, Johnny, you ought to know. Johnny Dunn. Johnny Dunn, the Florence Mills show was downtown, you know. And he got off and Johnny, he was sharp dressed, you know, he's standing up there with his coat on, you know, and a cane, no hat, hair shining like a onion, you know. He's looking at Louis and it was early in the evening and Ron McGaugh's out there doing this motelie. I think he knew about this. I believe he knew about this. I believe he knew. And Johnny's standing up there, standing with his arm on the bandstand, see they had a railing around us, you know. And so all of a sudden he says to Louis, hey give me that horn. Look, give it to him. Give it to him. In the first place, Louis was fooling around with the horn. He didn't have the A shank pulled out, you know. And Johnny, he ain't did nothing, you know. But when that man gave Louis that horn back, it was awful. I felt like hiding myself. You know, it was one of them things, you know. He made him look bad. Oh, it looked terrible. He should never did that. Made who look bad, Louis? Johnny Dunn. Louis made Johnny look bad.
